o1.biggest_strength: It builds bundles from the pairs customers already buy, then ties the shipping decision to COD/RTO economics with break-evens and a practical test plan.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some projection maths is compressed and slightly opaque, especially the Glow Routine break-even increment and the lip-balm cart lift, so the team would need to re-check those assumptions before quoting them.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: A one-page reconciliation table showing each bundle’s margin, break-even, threshold effect and COD impact, with cleaner assumptions and no ambiguous incremental-profit figures.

o2.biggest_strength: The serum-to-serum-plus-lip-to-routine ladder is a strong merchandising idea and the assumptions are stated clearly.
o2.biggest_mistake: The ₹599 threshold maths is materially off: it assumes only about 1,000 affected orders versus a likely much larger slice, and it counts lip-balm margin as gain while ignoring the lost ₹49 shipping fee, so the +₹28,000/month projection is not reliable.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Rebuild the threshold P&L from the order export, net off lost shipping fees and COD RTO, and add explicit COD handling plus a clearer body/second-category bundle.

reason: Output 1 is the one I would hand to my team tomorrow: it uses our real buying patterns, accounts for COD/RTO, gives a defensible shipping line and has testable stop rules. Output 2 has a nice ladder, but the ₹599 shipping maths has material errors that could lead us into a bad launch decision.
